verdict_reason: The design is directionally sound but carries three major defects (score formula conflates volume with quality, diversity-first can force a floor-scored lab representative over a stronger same-lab alternative, and -Role lacks name validation against path traversal) plus several minor integration gaps with the hook parser, the roster validator, and -Require semantics that should be resolved before implementation.
reply_markdown:
## Framing challenge first

The brief presupposes epsilon-greedy weighted draws. Options it does not list:

- **A. Ratings stay advisory.** Keep roster order as the coordinator's explicit ranking (Select-RosterReviewer already embodies it); ratings only feed the scoreboard humans read. No RNG, no routing record, no reproducibility machinery. Correct choice if rating volume is low.
- **B. Thompson sampling** with a Beta prior per (lineage, purpose) instead of fixed 0.2 epsilon-greedy: solves Q1 and Q2 together (decay falls out of the posterior), at similar code size.
- **C. Judge-picked panel**: a cheap model reads the scoreboard JSON and picks members. Reuses existing infrastructure, no formula to tune, but non-deterministic and harder to test with fakes.

To choose I would need: monthly rating volume per lineage (if under a few dozen, all scoring is noise and A wins); whether the operator values reproducible draws over adaptivity; quota cost of the default panel sizes.

## Q1 - score formula
Not sane as specified. Additive `1 + yes + 0.5*partly - no` rewards volume, not quality: a busy reviewer at 80% yes (20 ratings) outranks a perfect one with 3 ratings ~17:3 in draw weight. The purpose fallback makes it worse: the all-purpose score folds in chore ratings and the +1 baseline, so a good chore reviewer inherits an inflated framing score. `-Useful no` requires `-Note` (codex-findings.ps1:118), so negatives are costlier to record - an upward bias the formula does not correct. Prefer a rate with a confidence prior: `(yes + 0.5*partly + k*0.7) / (n + k)`, k around 3-5, which pulls sparse lineages to neutral and makes the 90-day window the only decay knob. The floor 0.25 is fine as a keep-exploring weight under either formula.

## Q2 - exploration 0.2
Right order of magnitude: a roster of ~10, k=3, a few panels a day gives an unrated reviewer a slot roughly every 1-2 days. Yes, decay it - a constant 0.2 keeps wasting a fifth of slots on known-bad reviewers after hundreds of ratings. Thompson sampling (option B) gives decay for free; under epsilon-greedy, scale epsilon by `1/sqrt(total ratings)` with a floor near 0.05.

## Q3 - diversity before rank
Yes, the regret case exists and is structural: with the 0.25 floor, a lab whose only representative was rated all `no` is still guaranteed a slot over a 2.0 second member of a strong lab. Guard: diversity applies only among entries scoring >= neutral (1.0); below that, fall back to pure rank. Separately, `lab` defaulting to the provider label mis-fires for agy entries, whose label is free text (common.ps1:4540) - two Google models under two labels count as two labs while sharing one quota.

## Q4 - roles vs presets
Prompt-only. Effort and max words are per-purpose and mapped through endpoint vocabularies (codex-consult.ps1:713-737, Resolve-EffortPlan); letting a role raise effort breaks the caps story and the ledger's comparability. If a role needs more room later, add a role-specific max-words override, never effort.

## Q5 - out per entry or per group
Judge per endpoint group, display per entry. Health is already keyed on the provider fingerprint (Get-EndpointHealth, common.ps1:4425) and Get-PanelPlan already merges labels sharing a fingerprint - two agy models share one Google sign-in, so one 429 means both are out; per-entry independent judgment would be wrong. The one-line format holds by compressing shared-quota entries (`gemini :: *`) and naming only what is OUT. Note the roster walk already refuses unknown-reset quota endpoints for 60 min (common.ps1:4801); only the codex-providers display (lines 252/295 require QuotaKnown) lags - the addendum is a display change, not new availability logic.

## Requested checks
RC1: in the repo root, run `pwsh -NoProfile -File plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-scoreboard.ps1 -Json` (read-only, ~10 s) and count ratings per lineage: if the busiest lineage has <30 ratings, finding #1 settles toward a rate-with-prior or toward option A (ratings advisory only).
RC2: read the maintainer's roster file (`$env:CODEX_CONSULT_ROSTER` or ~/.codex/codex-consult-roster.json, read-only) and list the agy labels: two labels on one lab confirms finding #2's lab-default defect.

findings.claim: The R15 score formula (1 + yes + 0.5*partly - no, floor 0.25) conflates rating volume with quality, and the all-purpose fallback inherits unrelated-purpose ratings plus the +1 baseline; ratings do record `when` (codex-findings.ps1:410) so the 90-day window is implementable, but the formula itself mis-ranks.
findings.trigger: Two lineages on one purpose: 20 ratings at 80% yes vs 3 ratings at 100% yes - the former draws at roughly 17:3 odds despite the lower rate.

evidence.observation: A rating stores n, consult_id, lineage, provider, model, purpose, useful, note, when - timestamps exist, topics do not.
-Useful no requires -Note, so negative ratings cost more to record than positive ones.
Ratings aggregate per (lineage, purpose) across all task stores; no rate or confidence normalization anywhere.

findings.verification: Compute both formulas over the real findings.json ratings (RC1) and compare the resulting draw-weight ratios per lineage.
findings.remedy: Use a rate with a confidence prior: (yes + 0.5*partly + k*0.7)/(n + k), k ~3-5, floored at 0.25; apply the same formula to the all-purpose fallback.

findings.claim: Diversity-before-rank guarantees a panel slot to a lab whose only representative sits at the 0.25 floor (rated all 'no'), displacing a strong second member of another lab; additionally the lab default (provider label) misfires for agy entries whose label is free text - one lab can occupy two 'labs' while sharing one quota.
findings.trigger: Roster with labs A (two entries, scores 2.0 and 1.8) and B (one entry, score 0.25), panel size 2: B's 0.25 entry is picked over A's 1.8 entry.

evidence.observation: For agy the provider is a free label and two entries with the same label and different models are allowed - nothing ties labels to real labs.

evidence.reference: brief design item 2 plus the 0.25 score floor
evidence.observation: The floor keeps every lab eligible regardless of track record, and diversity runs before rank.

findings.verification: With fakes, construct the trigger roster and confirm the picked pair under the specified algorithm.
findings.remedy: Apply diversity only among entries scoring >= the neutral score; below that, fill by rank. Canonicalize lab values (lowercase, known-lab alias table) and validate against the alias table, not just non-empty.

findings.claim: -Role <name> loads templates/role-<name>.md but the design never specifies name validation; 'unknown role refused' implies file-existence lookup, which without slug validation permits path traversal (-Role ../brief reads templates/../brief.md, and worse with .collab/roles/ roots).

evidence.observation: The role block path is name-templated and the only stated validation is 'unknown role refused'; the codebase's existing validators (roster keys, -Task slug in codex-scoreboard.ps1:67) show the project treats slug validation as necessary elsewhere.

findings.verification: After implementation, run the bridge with -Role ../x against fakes and confirm refusal.
findings.remedy: Validate the role name as a slug (letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore, no separators) before any path join, matching the -Task rule in codex-scoreboard.ps1:67.

findings.claim: The hook parses codex-providers verdicts with the regex ^(available|unavailable|unknown) - the addendum's new 'out - ... (until ...)' line and relative hints will not parse; the addendum never mentions updating the parser, so the sharpened line degrades to 'reviewer check failed'.
findings.trigger: Any endpoint out with the new -Short output format.

evidence.observation: Verdict regex accepts only available|unavailable|unknown with an optional parenthesized reason.

findings.verification: Run the hook against a ledger containing a fresh quota failure after the format change.
findings.remedy: Extend the hook parser (or give -Short a dedicated JSON mode) in the same wave as the new line format.

findings.claim: Addendum item 9's 'quota without known reset marks the endpoint out for 60 minutes' already exists for the roster walk (Get-PreflightVerdict -RosterWalk refuses it, common.ps1:4801-4806); only the codex-providers display lags (lines 252/295 require QuotaKnown). The design should state it is a display change, or the rule risks being implemented twice and diverging.
findings.trigger: BytePlus-style 429 without a reset time: the panel already skips the entry while the hook reports it available.

evidence.observation: RosterWalk marks a <=60-min-old quota failure without reset time unavailable.
Display downgrades to unavailable only when $health.QuotaKnown (a retry_after exists).

findings.verification: Record a quota failure without retry_after via fakes; observe skipped in the walk but 'available' from codex-providers.
findings.remedy: Reword item 9 as aligning codex-providers/-Short and the hook with the existing RosterWalk rule; reuse Get-PreflightVerdict's reason strings.

findings.claim: Design item 6 contradicts itself - equal weights still shuffle, yet with no ratings the order is documented as roster order even though no ratings is exactly the equal-weights case - and it creates a discontinuity: the first rating recorded anywhere flips every panel from deterministic roster order to shuffled draws.
findings.trigger: The first -Rate ever recorded in a repository.

evidence.observation: The parenthetical asks 'draw with equal weights = roster order? No' and then documents roster order for the no-ratings case.

findings.verification: Fakes: run a panel before and after recording one rating; diff the picked order distribution.
findings.remedy: Pick one rule: either always shuffle (simplest, documented), or weight by score only once a lineage clears a minimum rating count, blending into roster order as the prior.

findings.claim: The seeded draw's reproducibility depends on how the string panel id becomes an RNG seed; .NET string.GetHashCode() is randomized per process, so a naive seeding makes 'same seed -> same pick' fail across runs. Also, reproducibility only holds for a frozen eligible/score snapshot - new ratings change picks for the same seed; the routing record mitigates forensically but the test claim needs the caveat.
findings.trigger: Replaying a recorded seed in a new process after GetHashCode-based seeding.

evidence.observation: The seed is 'the panel id' (a string); PowerShell Get-Random -SetSeed takes an int, forcing a hash the design does not specify.

findings.verification: Unit test: same panel id seeded in two separate pwsh processes must produce the same pick.
findings.remedy: Specify a stable hash (e.g. first 8 bytes of SHA-256 of the panel id) as the seed, and document that reproducibility is per recorded eligible set.

findings.claim: -Roles a,b,c assigns roles 'in order to the picked members', but picked order is now the seeded draw order, so role assignment is a lottery: an edge-cases or security role can land on the floor-scored member, which inverts the intent of giving narrow roles to suitable reviewers.
findings.trigger: -Panel -Roles security,tests with a draw that picks the weakest member first.

evidence.observation: Item 8 defines assignment by picked order; item 6 makes picked order draw-determined.

findings.verification: Fakes: two seeds, same roles; check which lineage receives the security role.
findings.remedy: Assign roles by score rank among picked members, or allow explicit lineage=role pairs in the roster.

findings.claim: -Require defines refusal BEFORE anything starts but not failure after start: today a member failing at launch is recorded skipped and the panel proceeds (exit 0 only when all usable, exit 1 otherwise, codex-consult.ps1:1530-1531). Whether a required member's mid-panel failure aborts the panel or merely downgrades the exit code is unspecified.
findings.trigger: A required reviewer's quota is hit between the -Require check and its slot in Get-PanelPlan serialization.

evidence.observation: Exit code reflects all-usable only; the run completes with skipped members.
Stop-WithError exits 1; exit 5 is a new code that must be documented (codex-providers.ps1:381 already uses exit 3).

findings.verification: Fakes: required member available at check time, failing at launch; observe bridge behavior against the specified rule.
findings.remedy: Specify: a required member that fails after start aborts the panel at the next slot boundary with exit 5, and the ledger records the required set.

findings.claim: The roster validator refuses unknown keys (common.ps1:4616 top level, 4635 per entry), so the design's lab field, require defaults, and ledger topics all need whitelist updates the design never lists; and a typo'd lineage in a require default silently never matches any entry, disabling the guard without error.
findings.trigger: Roster gains "lab" before the validator is updated: every run refuses with 'unknown key'.

evidence.observation: Top-level whitelist: roster_version, reviewers, parallel only.
Per-entry whitelist: provider, model, codex_config, auth, panel, engine.

findings.verification: Add a lab key to a test roster and load it at HEAD: expect refusal.
findings.remedy: List the validator changes in the design, and validate require lineages against the roster at load (unknown lineage = roster error).

findings.claim: Ratings store no topics; topic attribution depends on joining consult_id to the ledger's new topics[], but the scoreboard's fallback path (rating's own purpose field when n is not in the ledger, line 177-180) has no topic equivalent - older or pruned ledger entries silently lose topic attribution, and the design does not say where selection-time scoring lives, risking drift between the bridge's scoring and the scoreboard's -By topic aggregation.
findings.trigger: -Topic on a consultation whose ledger entry is later unreadable: the rating counts for the purpose but not the topic.

evidence.observation: The rating record has no topics field.
Ratings fall back to their own purpose field when the ledger join fails.

findings.verification: Rate a topic'd consultation, remove the ledger entry in a fake store, run -By topic.
findings.remedy: Copy topics[] onto the rating record at -Rate time, and put the scoring function in codex-consult-common.ps1 so the bridge and the scoreboard share it.

findings.claim: Panel size counts members that will RUN at selection time, but availability can change before launch (quota hit mid-panel), so a sized panel can still run short with no backfill; and the floor warning fires on every deliberate -PanelSize 1 framing/decision run, nagging the explicit choice it should respect.
findings.trigger: -PanelSize 3 where the third member's endpoint hits its limit after the first two launch.

evidence.reference: brief design items 1 and 3 plus Get-PanelPlan serialization
evidence.observation: Sizing happens at selection; serialized per-endpoint execution leaves a window for state change.

findings.verification: Fakes: fail a mid-panel member and check whether the panel backfills or runs short.
findings.remedy: Document the no-backfill semantics (or backfill from the eligible rest), and suppress the floor warning when -PanelSize was given explicitly.

unproven: Actual monthly rating volume per lineage in the maintainer's repositories - settles whether any scoring beats roster order (RC1).
The maintainer roster's real agy labels - settles how often the lab-default misfires (RC2).
The intended string-to-int seeding for the panel id - finding #7 assumes GetHashCode risk, not confirmed.
Whether the panel id exists before selection in the bridge's flow (routing needs it as the seed).
